task.description:
ELIXIR-DEV completed the rework REVIEWER requested in handoffs/WF02-REQ197-20260830/step-02a-elixir-dev-rework1.json (REVIEWER's own step-02d BLOCKER, this same gate, FAILED verdict recorded in this file's prior revision before being overwritten with this fresh PENDING request). This is rework addressing REVIEWER's specific signed-infinity/NaN finding -- not a new SECURITY-REVIEWER pass, since REVIEWER's own gate is what failed last time and SECURITY-REVIEWER already PASSED this diff's scope/invariant checks in step-02c with no BLOCKER. Re-check this same REVIEWER gate.

What changed since REVIEWER's FAIL verdict: implemented design doc §4.3/§4.6's already-specified signed-infinity/NaN 3-way split exactly as REVIEWER's rework handoff described, now unblocked by REVIEWER's own OQ-1 sign-off.

1. `infinity_marker()` (expr.ex:99) extended from `:infinity` to `:infinity | :neg_infinity | :nan`. The @typedoc directly above it (expr.ex:82-98) rewritten to state the gate is RESOLVED (rework iteration 2) rather than leaving stale 'not implemented yet, pending REVIEWER sign-off' language.

2. `apply_float_arith/3`'s `:div` clauses (expr.ex:1107-1115) implement the 3-way dividend-sign split per design §4.3: dividend == 0.0 and divisor == 0.0 -> {:ok, :nan} (checked first); dividend > 0.0 and divisor == 0.0 -> {:ok, :infinity}; dividend < 0.0 and divisor == 0.0 -> {:ok, :neg_infinity}; non-zero divisor unchanged (native float division).

3. `apply_neg/1` (expr.ex:1121-1129) gains clauses per design §4.4: :infinity <-> :neg_infinity flip on negation; :nan negated stays :nan.

4. The ordering-comparison eval clause (expr.ex:1005-1043) now implements design §4.6's full 5-clause guard order exactly as specified: (1) nil-check (unchanged, pre-existing) -> {:ok, nil}; (2) NEW :nan guard -- either operand :nan -> {:ok, false} for every ordering operator, including :nan vs :nan; (3) infinity-marker branch, now covering both :infinity and :neg_infinity via `lv in [:infinity, :neg_infinity]` / `rv in [:infinity, :neg_infinity]`, delegating to apply_ordering/3; (4) is_number guard (subsumed into clause 3's combined guard, unchanged semantics); (5) type-mismatch fallback (unchanged). Confirmed nil, :nan, and the infinity markers are mutually exclusive operand shapes, so this guard order cannot shadow anything, matching design §4.6's own reasoning.

5. `apply_ordering/3` (expr.ex:1141-1152) extended: :infinity is the greatest possible value, :neg_infinity the least, both directions handled (l or r being either marker), :nan never reaches this function since eval/2's ordering clause filters it out first via guard (2) above.

6. Equality (==/!=) eval clause (expr.ex:998-1012) gains the design's stated :nan override: :nan == :nan is {:ok, false}, :nan != :nan (or vs. anything) is {:ok, true} -- checked ahead of the pre-existing generic lv == rv / lv != rv clause, since plain Elixir atom equality would otherwise wrongly say :nan == :nan is true.

7. New tests added to test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs (none existed before for the signed/NaN cases -- describe block 'eval/2 -- signed float division-by-zero (REQ-197 §4.3, OQ-1 sign-flip fix)', after the existing 'eval/2 -- undefined variable and type-mismatch errors (AC3)' describe block): positive-dividend/zero-divisor -> :infinity (re-asserts AC4's existing case, still passes unmodified); negative-dividend/zero-divisor -> :neg_infinity; 0.0/0.0 -> :nan; :nan compared via every ordering operator (including :nan vs :nan) is false; :nan == :nan is false and :nan != :nan is true; and two REGRESSION tests demonstrating REVIEWER's exact sign-flip finding is fixed -- one at the eval/2 level (`amount / divisor < threshold` with amount=-1000.0, divisor=0.0, threshold=100.0, now {:ok, true} where :neg_infinity < 100.0 is correctly true) and one at the evaluate_condition/2 gateway level using the CEL-syntax condition string `variables.amount / variables.divisor > 100.0` with the same negative amount and zero divisor, now correctly false via Expr.evaluate_condition/2 (was wrongly true under the old unsigned-only :infinity-is-greatest fallback).

No other section of expr.ex or the design doc was touched: OQ-4 (negative-operand integer div/mod rounding direction) was left as awareness-only per REVIEWER's own carry-forward instruction, and the parse_strict/1 tokenizer-duplication design-preference deviation was left as-is (already ACCEPTED by REVIEWER as a reasonable tradeoff in the prior pass) -- neither was re-opened or re-negotiated.
acceptance_criteria: infinity_marker() type is `:infinity | :neg_infinity | :nan` (expr.ex:99) and the @typedoc above it (expr.ex:82-98) states the gate is resolved, with no stale 'pending REVIEWER sign-off' / 'not implemented yet' language remaining.

apply_float_arith/3's :div clauses implement the exact 3-way dividend-sign split: dividend > 0.0, divisor == 0.0 -> {:ok, :infinity}; dividend < 0.0, divisor == 0.0 -> {:ok, :neg_infinity}; dividend == 0.0, divisor == 0.0 -> {:ok, :nan}.
apply_neg/1 correctly flips :infinity <-> :neg_infinity and leaves :nan as :nan.

The ordering-comparison eval clause and apply_ordering/3 implement design §4.6's 5-clause guard order exactly, with :neg_infinity as the least value and :infinity the greatest in every ordering comparison, and :nan self-unequal/incomparable (always false for <, <=, >, >=, including nan vs nan).
Equality (==/!=) involving :nan overrides plain Elixir atom equality: :nan == :nan is false, :nan != :nan is true.

New regression test(s) in test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs prove REVIEWER's exact sign-flip finding is fixed: a negative-amount float division by zero, compared against a finite positive threshold, now evaluates correctly (both an eval/2-level `<` case and an evaluate_condition/2-level `>` gateway case are covered).
Existing AC4 test (positive dividend / 0.0 -> :infinity) still passes unmodified.
expr.ex's documented purity grep (moduledoc's own command) returns zero matches -- confirmed by direct grep invocation, real output quoted below.

mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted, and mix test test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs all pass -- real output quoted below, not asserted from memory.

No scope creep: only lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex and test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs were touched in this rework pass (test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs was re-run for regression coverage but not modified); OQ-4 and the parse_strict/1 duplication question were not re-opened.
CRITICAL: this handoff's top-level status field is exactly PENDING (grepped and confirmed before commit, per this project's own recurring anti-pattern entry on this exact mistake).
